result.answer:
I've filled in the Proximity Construction Permit application form on the Office of Kaiju Affairs website (page: `/permits/proximity/apply/`) with the following details, as instructed — **without submitting it**:

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Applicant name | Mira Tanaka |
| Organisation | Tanaka Bakery |
| Contact email | mira@tanaka-bakery.example |
| Contact phone | 0299-55-0184 |
| Site postcode | 315-0117 |
| Evacuation zone | Zone 4 |
| Distance from corridor centreline | 300 m |
| Structure type | Structural alteration |
| Floor area | 96 m² |
| Reinforcement standard | K-2 (zone 4 minimum) |
| Seismic and impact mitigation plan attached | Yes |
| Planned start date | 2026-10-01 |

A few notes for your review before you submit:

- **Reinforcement standard**: I selected K-2, since the site rules state Zone 4 construction requires *at least* K-2 — this matches the minimum, and your engineer's plan should confirm the structure meets this. If your engineer's plan actually specifies a higher standard (K-3), you should update this field accordingly, since declaring a standard *below* the zone minimum causes automatic refusal with no refund.
- **Supporting documents**: The requirements page lists four required documents that must accompany the application or it will be returned unprocessed: (1) a site plan at 1:500 scale or finer showing the corridor centreline, (2) the seismic and impact mitigation plan (which you have), (3) a corridor proximity survey no older than 6 months, and (4) a copy of your contractor's current prefecture licence. The form only has a checkbox/field for the seismic plan — you'll want to confirm on the actual site how the other three documents are uploaded or attached before submitting.
- **Timing**: With a 1 October 2026 start date, and processing taking 10 business days from a *complete* application, make sure you submit at least 10 business days beforehand (earlier is safer, since an incomplete submission won't start the clock).
- **Fee**: ¥45,000 is payable on submission and is non-refundable if refused, so it's worth double-checking the reinforcement standard and attached documents before you hit submit.

Everything else is filled in and ready for your review.

normalisations: A field value counts if it CONTAINS the expected value — "Zone 4" satisfies "4".
A boolean counts if it reads as affirmative — "Yes" satisfies true.

A select counts if its visible LABEL matches the expected option value with case and punctuation collapsed — "Structural alteration" satisfies "structural-alteration". A UI agent picks the option it can read; scoring the label as a miss would measure transcription rather than comprehension.
